name: Whiskey Sour
description: Bourbon, lemon, and sugar—optionally with egg white for a silky foam.
history: A foundational sour from the 19th century. The egg-white Boston Sour variation became common later; both are legitimate.
whyItWorks: Lemon cuts whiskey’s sweetness while sugar restores balance. Egg white adds texture without changing the core flavor arc.

ingredients.label: Egg white (optional)
ingredients.notes: Skip if unavailable; the drink remains a proper Whiskey Sour.
Dash across the foam if using egg white.

steps: If using egg white, dry-shake all ingredients without ice for 10 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard until cold.
Strain over fresh ice in a rocks glass, or up into a coupe.
Garnish with lemon and cherry; add bitters dots on foam if present.
techniqueNotes: Without egg white, a single hard shake is enough.
Russell’s Reserve or Eagle Rare both shine here.

recommendedBottles.rationale: Balanced oak and caramel that hold up to lemon.
Fruitier bourbon for a softer sour.
Familiar spice and structure for an everyday sour.

substitutions.notes: Rye sour is spicier and drier.
